冒 expresses braving danger or venturing despite difficulty in 冒す (おかす) and 冒険 (ぼうけん), "adventure; risky venture." It is not a general label for anything dangerous: 危険 (きけん) names danger, while 危険を冒す (きけんをおかす) means taking a risk.

Modern-shape mnemonic: picture an eye, 目, beneath a boxlike upper outline, looking ahead despite danger. This is a memory aid, not a historical sun-plus-eye explanation. The classical indexing radical is 冂, not 日, even though the upper shape can resemble 日.
Both complete source readings are retained and selected for reading practice.

Do not force the risk-taking gloss into every compound: 冒頭 names an opening, not an adventure. 冒す also has a harm/affliction sense: 病に冒される (やまいにおかされる), "be afflicted by a disease," is passive, not someone choosing to take a risk.

犯 also has the reading おか.す, but 犯す is used for committing an offense, as in 罪を犯す (つみをおかす), "commit a crime." 侵す (おかす) concerns invading or infringing and can overlap with 冒す in harm/affliction uses. These are useful spelling distinctions, not perfectly separate meaning compartments. For shape comparison, 官 has a roof and a different connected lower outline; neither 官 nor 目 means braving danger.

冒す おかす — brave danger; venture despite difficulty
冒す means braving danger or proceeding despite a known difficulty. In 危険を冒す (きけんをおかす), "take a risk," を marks the danger being faced. It is a transitive verb, not a noun meaning an adventure.
危険を冒して山に登りました。 (きけんをおかしてやまにのぼりました。) — I climbed the mountain despite the danger.
危険を冒す必要はありません。 (きけんをおかすひつようはありません。) — There is no need to take a risk.
The second sentence says that taking the risk is unnecessary; it does not say that the situation is safe.
冒 writes おか, with す as okurigana. There is no second kanji to read as a compound. This is a godan verb: 冒します (おかします), 冒して (おかして), 冒さない (おかさない).

冒険 (ぼうけん) is the related noun "adventure; risky venture"; 冒険する means to venture or have an adventure. 危険 (きけん) names danger, whether or not anyone chooses to face it. Avoiding danger contrasts with braving it, but 冒す has other senses too, so no single opposite covers every use.

Do not translate every occurrence as voluntarily taking a risk. 病に冒される (やまいにおかされる), "be afflicted by a disease," uses the passive of the harm/affliction sense. Here the person is affected by the illness, not choosing to brave it. This sense can also concern harmful chemicals. The dictionary also records desecrating something sacred and assuming someone else's surname; these are separate senses, not explanations of 危険を冒す.

Two other verbs share the reading おかす. 犯す, written with 犯, is used in 罪を犯す (つみをおかす), "commit a crime." 侵す concerns invading or infringing and also has a harm/affliction use overlapping with 冒す. Choose the spelling from the expression and meaning, not from the sound alone; this comparison is not an absolute division of every use.
